key_insight: Pay for higher-fidelity LLM outputs when downstream optimization accuracy warrants it; adaptive oracle switching can match or beat the cumulative cost of the best fixed oracle in hindsight under the known-bias framework.
engineering_relevance: Cost-aware fidelity selection can reduce spending on LLM-assisted data curation while targeting the accuracy needed by downstream optimization.
method: Known bias: use a restarted, cost-aware policy to select oracle fidelity across optimization stages.
Unknown bias: periodically evaluate trusted gradients to certify progress and eliminate unsuccessful oracle sources.
Instantiate the frameworks with biased stochastic gradient extrapolation and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise.
evidence_signal: Synthetic and LLM-completion experiments show adaptive switching skipping several expensive LLM oracles and substantially reducing cumulative cost versus fixed high-fidelity alternatives at comparable accuracy.
watch_item: Unknown-bias deployment requires trusted-gradient evaluations, with an explicit tradeoff between certification cost and delayed detection of biased sources.
paper_title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
